top.reason: detach passes a newly bound function to off, so it does not remove the listener registered in attach and messages continue reaching the disposed handler.
Concurrent take calls can read the same token count before either write completes, then both store the same decremented state and both allow a request when only one token exists.
The sort comparator returns only true or false instead of a signed ordering value, so some valid input orders remain non-descending despite the newest-first contract.
for...in supplies index as a string, so index + 1 produces ranks such as "01" and "11" instead of the documented numeric 1-based ranks.
When ping rejects, the interval ignores the async callback's rejected promise and healthy remains true, contradicting the requirement that a failed ping mark the connection unhealthy.
Subtracting an extra 1 makes lastN return n+1 visits whenever more than n visits exist; for three visits and n=1 it returns two.
The intentionally detached deliveries catch and log their own failures, matching the documented best-effort contract.
Per-account promise chaining serializes each read-modify-write operation, preserves each caller's result, and safely cleans up the completed queue.
The inclusive loop and count formula agree for both ordered and empty ranges.
Each comparator implements its documented order, and standard JavaScript sorting preserves score ties.
When interval fetches overlap, an earlier request can resolve after a later one and overwrite its newer items, so the snapshot exposes stale data instead of the latest poll result.
The optional address and theme fields are guarded with defaults before use.

top.reason: detach() passes a new bound function to off(), so the registered listener remains and continues calling the disposed handler after detachment.
Concurrent take() calls can read the same token count, both return true, and overwrite it with the same decrement, allowing more successful requests than capacity.
The comparator returns boolean 0/1 instead of a signed ordering; for [older, newer] it compares them as equal and leaves the older post first.
for...in supplies string indices, so index + 1 concatenates and returns ranks such as "01" and "11" instead of numeric 1 and 2.
When ping() rejects, the interval ignores the async callback's rejected promise and never marks healthy false, leaving a failed connection available and causing an unhandled rejection.
The extra -1 makes lastN return one too many visits; with two visits and n=1 it slices from index 0 and returns both.
The unawaited delivery is documented best-effort behavior, and each send rejection is caught and logged inside its async callback.
Per-account promise chaining serializes reads and writes, and cleanup only removes the current queue tail.
Both functions consistently implement ranges inclusive of the documented endpoints.
Each comparator implements its documented ordering, and a zero score difference preserves tie order under stable Array sorting.
Overlapping interval fetches can resolve out of order, allowing an older poll to overwrite a newer successful result and reset its failure state.
No runtime defect is demonstrated for values permitted by the declared Profile contract.
